They navigate a low-dimensional persona space....
rawContent:
Tweet by @muratcan (Muratcan Koylan)
Author bio: Member of Technical Staff (Agents), Research @sullyai 

Building AI medical employees

Prev/ AI Persona Development & Research @ 99Ravens
Text: LLMs don’t “have a personality.”

They navigate a low-dimensional persona space. Roughly 4–19 axes explain ~70% of role variance.

Construction: which region you want (who + how)
Stabilization: keeping it there when the next user turn pulls elsewhere

Most persona prompts only do the first. That’s why they feel sharp on turn 1 and mushy a few turns later.

Thin layers like “You are a helpful X” mostly reinforce an already-strong attractor: the default Assistant (consultant / analyst / generalist tropes).

Don't only write “You are an ad writer.” 

Put the persona on 2–3 trait axes:

Role: performance ad writer for B2B SaaS; Meta/LinkedIn feed ads, not brand films.

Traits: concrete, benefit-first, slightly irreverent, short-line rhythm, not Mad Men poet, not brand strategist deck-writer, not “as an AI I can help brainstorm messaging” chatbot.

Desired neighbors: direct-response copywriter, offer architect, headline mechanic.

Forbidden neighbors: brand storyteller, vibe poet, polite marketing assistant.

Also: “somewhat” vs “fully” role-play is real. 

Unsteered models often stay somewhat Assistant-adjacent (“I’m an AI that can help with legal questions”). Full embodiment means overpowering that attractor with denser identity context.

Task framing is persona control.

- Want a reliable specialist documenter? Bounded task + refinement + schema. Don’t invite phenomenology or “be the doctor’s empathy.”

- Want voice / creative depth? You need the off-axis pull.  authorial voice, inhabit, texture. Then construct the destination hard enough that drift lands there, not in generic theatrical mush.

- Writing help stays Assistant-like until someone asks for a specific creative voice. 

For every persona, run an association audit:
> Desired neighbor roles/traits
> Forbidden neighbor roles/traits
> Hard situations where the wrong neighbor activates (emotion, meta, creative voice)

And a usable pipeline for writing personas:
1. Role/trait description
2. Generate 5 system-prompt variants (not one)
3. Elicitation questions that force the persona to show itself
4. Judge rubric: full / somewhat / none (or 0–100 trait strength)
5. Keep only prompts that actually move behavior
6. Contrast: positive elicitation vs negative suppression

Basically DSPy/eval-loop prompt design, with persona as the metric.
